result.summary:
Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0458-20260904/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json in full. ISSUE-FIXER recommended instrumented/superseded_by:ISS-0219 (citing ISS-0217/ISS-0110 as tighter mechanism matches). Independently verified this against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's actual definitions rather than accepting the recommendation as-is: instrumented requires (a) this run shipped real verified work, and (b) superseded_by names a successor CARRYING REMAINING WORK. Checked ISS-0219/ISS-0217/ISS-0110's own status fields directly (grep) -- all three are status: resolved, not open, unlike today's ISS-0456->ISS-0418 precedent where ISS-0418 is open with genuinely pending OQ-5 work. Considered whether this makes instrumented/superseded_by inapplicable (a dead-end pointer) or whether ISS-0114's own precedent (superseded_by: ISS-0110, written while ISS-0110 was open; ISS-0110 has SINCE resolved, and nobody backfilled or corrected ISS-0114's pointer for that) settles it -- concluded ISS-0114 establishes that a superseded_by pointer's validity is judged at the moment it is written, not by whether the target later closes, so pointing at ISS-0219 (this filing's own named candidate and the project's standing cross-reference for this connection-budget/contention class) is consistent with existing practice, not a new interpretation invented for this run. Also considered no_defect: rejected, because ISSUE_QUEUE.md's no_defect bar requires the investigation to establish NO root cause exists, and the opposite is true here -- a real, already-documented root cause (TenantSchemaReaper's liveness-guard race, ISS-0110's own targeted reproduction of a byte-for-byte-identical 42P01 signature) demonstrably exists. instrumented is therefore the correct status, with the caveat (stated explicitly in the yaml's resolution_note) that this run itself shipped no new artefact -- the 'verified work' the status format nominally expects is the ALREADY-SHIPPED work under ISS-0219/ISS-0217/ISS-0110, re-confirmed live by this run's own reproduction attempts, not new work produced in this run.

Wrote docs/issues/ISS-0458.yaml: status instrumented, superseded_by ISS-0219, resolved_in_run/resolved_at set, related: [ISS-0219, ISS-0217, ISS-0110, ISS-0113], full resolution_note citing the diagnosis's evidence (two isolated 56/56 runs, one 3214/3214 four-way-parallel full-suite run, ISS-0110's own corroborating byte-for-byte-identical error signature, the ISS-0427/PR#881 orthogonality reasoning) and explicitly stating what remains unclosed.

Verified post-close via `gh issue view 882 --json state,closedByPullRequestsReferences,comments`: state CLOSED, last comment matches exactly what was posted (quoted in full in this run's shell history). No linked/merged PR closes this issue (closedByPullRequestsReferences empty) -- the --comment path is the one satisfied, which is sufficient per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's either/or evidence rule.

Released queue task 458 via release_lock with NO status field (agent_id tvolodi-orch) -- confirmed via the response body: status now 'open', locked_by null, locked_at null. This is deliberate, not an oversight: TASK_QUEUE.md's release_lock section is explicit that status:"done" asserts the underlying defect is fixed, which is false here -- nothing was fixed in this run, the existing fixes for this recurrence class already shipped under separate, already-closed issues. Matches today's own WF03-ISS0456-20260904 precedent exactly (also instrumented/superseded_by, also released without status).
